title: Maná Is Bringing Its Spectacular Red Rocks Amphitheatre Concert to a Streamer
summary: Vivir Sin Aire Tour (Live from Red Rocks) will arrive in November accompanied by a mini-documentary.
contentText:
The spectacular concerts that Maná held in September at the iconic Red Rocks Amphitheatre are coming to YouTube for fans around the world to enjoy — and sooner than you think, Billboard can exclusively report on Tuesday (Oct. 27).

Maná : Vivir Sin Aire Tour (Live From Red Rocks) , presented by YouTube and Warner Music, will stream globally on Nov. 6 at 8:30 p.m. ET on the YouTube channel of the Mexican band, which is celebrating its 40th anniversary this year. Once the premiere concludes, the special will be available for on-demand viewing.

Located among the red monoliths of Morrison, Colo., the Red Rocks Amphitheatre is one of the most iconic rock venues in history, having hosted legends such as The Rolling Stones, Jimi Hendrix and Led Zeppelin. According to the press release, “performing on this mythical stage was more than a tour stop” for lead singer Fher Olvera — “it was the ultimate fulfillment of a youthful prophecy.”

The announcement of the premiere is accompanied by a mini-documentary that showcases Olvera’s deep emotional connection to this venue. In it, the singer recalls his days at 21 years old, when he lived in Denver and worked washing dishes. He would gaze at the imposing formations of Red Rocks and wonder: “What would it feel like to play there?”

Decades later, in front of an ecstatic crowd and as the frontman of one of the most successful Latin rock bands in history, he looks back at the Red Rocks and experiences a moment of profound emotion and gratitude, spontaneously saying: “Ay cabrón … llegaste” (“Damn … you made it”).

The concert film at Red Rocks was recorded during Maná’s performances on Sept. 4 and 5, 2026, as part of their Vivir Sin Aire World Tour.

The band — which is also comprised of drummer Alex González, guitarist Sergio Vallín and bassist Juan Calleros, Maná — formed in Guadalajara in 1986 and is known for hits such as “Corazón Espinado” with Santana, “Labios Compartidos” and “Rayando el Sol.” The group remains as relevant as ever, filling venues around the world and receiving accolades such as the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Award for Latin Pop Artist of the Year, Duo or Group.

This year, Maná was also featured on Billboard ’s list of The 50 Best Latin Rock Bands of All Time . In 2025, it made history as the first Spanish-language rock group to be nominated for the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

Maná’s tour continues in the United States, with shows in cities including Detroit, Houston and Austin, before heading to Colombia to kick off the Latin American stadium leg on Nov. 28.
